findings.title: forEach(async) is not awaited, so reschedule cancellations race the reschedule email
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the inner async work. The control flow continues to `await sendRequestRescheduleEmail(...)` and then returns from the mutation immediately, while calendar/video deletions are still in flight. Users will receive a "please reschedule" email and the function will report success while the original booking is still present on calendars/video providers, causing double-booking and stale availability. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

findings.title: forEach(async) is not awaited in reschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires off async calendar/video deletions but does not wait for them. The surrounding `try/catch` will not see rejections, and `Reschedule` returns `true` (success) before the cancellations actually complete. The previous code had the same shape but the operations were effectively fire-and-forget; now with `await getCalendar(...)` inside, the race window is larger and the lack of awaiting becomes a real correctness bug.

findings.title: forEach(async) is not awaited in reschedule
findings.body: Identical bug to `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` starts async calendar/video deletion work but never awaits it. The function returns before deletions finish and the try/catch around it cannot catch rejections.

findings.title: forEach(async) populates apiDeletes after Promise.all already ran
Calendar deletions changed from concurrent to sequential
getCalendarCredentials returns a Promise-wrapped calendar but stays synchronous
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now `async`, so inside `getCalendarCredentials` `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` is a `Promise<Calendar | null>`, and the objects returned (`{ integration, credential, calendar }`) now carry a Promise where callers historically got a `Calendar`. The only in-tree caller (`getConnectedCalendars`) was patched to `await item.calendar`, but the function is exported, is not marked `async`, and the field is named `calendar` rather than `calendarPromise`. This makes it very easy for other consumers (and future code) to access `item.calendar` synchronously and silently get a Promise, leading to runtime `TypeError: calendar.deleteEvent is not a function` or undefined behavior. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve calendars before returning, or rename the field and document the async contract.

findings.title: Calendar credentials fetched serially in getConnectedCalendars
findings.body: In `getConnectedCalendars`, after destructuring each item the code does `const calendar = await item.calendar;` inside `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async (item) => {...}))`. Because each `.map` callback awaits the dynamic import of the calendar app before continuing, the dynamic imports for different calendar credentials run effectively serially per Promise.all branch iteration (each callback awaits before the next iterates). Although the outer `Promise.all` runs them concurrently in theory, the code path through `getCalendar` is now an extra await inside every iteration, adding latency vs. issuing all dynamic imports in parallel (e.g. `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(item => item.calendar))` once, then proceed).
